Theme 096 · Camera & edit grammar

Whip Pan

The camera is a restless head turning between rooms of a 360° panorama: dashboards, the Acme Pulse room, the anomaly, the lockup. Each beat is joined by a 0.25 s whip that smears the world into horizontal streaks and lands sharp on the downbeat; a panorama strip and pan arrows mark where we are.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Panorama rooms — four scenes laid out on one 360° strip so every transition is a real pan
  • Directional blur — SVG feGaussianBlur with x-only deviation, the signature of the whip
  • Streak layer — coloured horizontal bars in brand hues that sell speed and hide the cut
  • Locked-off text layer — headlines never blur; only the world moves
  • Panorama strip — top HUD showing which room is on screen, the map of the edit
  • Pan arrows — coral arrows with angle and duration, making direction readable in a still

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Whip — x offset −1080 px in 0.25 s (one beat at 120 BPM) with power4.inOut; blur 0 → 46 → 0 peaking mid-move; the cut hides at peak blur
  • Land on the beat — the settle frame falls exactly on the downbeat; 2-frame overshoot (+14 px) then back, expo.out 0.2 s
  • Streak-to-rule — on the final landing, streaks shrink height 20 → 3 px over 0.5 s and snap to fixed y positions to become the tagline rules

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Whip pans turn a list of features into a sense of speed and presence: Pulse is always looking around, and the landing frame gets a small jolt of attention every time. They also hide cuts, so each room can be built separately. Risk: overuse turns the film into a travel reel, and strong blur is uncomfortable for some viewers.

Adapt to your product: Lay your product screens out left-to-right as rooms of one panorama (inbox, editor, report, lockup) and whip between them on the beat. Keep whip direction consistent (always right, one whip back for the “aha”) so the viewer’s mental map holds.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whip_pan (whip pan definition and use as a transition) · https://www.studiobinder.com/blog/swish-pan-whip-pan-definition-film/ (matching speed and direction on both sides to hide the cut) · https://www.studiobinder.com/camera-shots/camera-movements/whip-pan-shot/ (whip pan uses: urgency, transitions, combining with other moves)
